subject: languages
intro: Languages lead into work where communicating across tongues is the job: interpretation and translation, language teaching at every level, and guiding travellers through places where the language is spoken.

roles.title: Interpreters and Translators
roles.what: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another, working wherever meaning must survive the crossing — courts, hospitals, conferences, publishing and business.
roles.where: The CEFR ladder climbs from A1 everyday expressions to C2 differentiating finer shades of meaning in the most complex situations — exactly the two-way proficiency interpreters and translators sell.

roles.title: Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach languages and literature courses in languages other than English, including American Sign Language — university teachers who plan courses, assess proficiency and, typically, research the language and its literatures.
roles.where: Units A1 through C2 are the common reference levels university language courses are built around; the atlas extension on writing systems and the bilingual brain supplies the knowledge-about-language that advanced teaching assumes.

roles.title: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
roles.what: Teach one or more subjects to students at the secondary school level — for language specialists, planning lessons, setting and marking work and building pupils' ability to communicate in another language.
roles.where: The A1–B1 units cover the classroom repertoire a school teacher trains: introducing yourself, describing your background, handling routine tasks, and producing simple connected text on familiar topics.

roles.title: Tour Guides and Escorts
roles.what: Escort individuals or groups on sightseeing tours or through places of interest such as industrial establishments, public buildings and art galleries, narrating as they go.
roles.where: The framework's B1 descriptor — dealing with most situations likely to arise whilst travelling in an area where the language is spoken — is a guide's daily reality; C1 fluency adds presenting places spontaneously.
